readme.saveNote: This package is a save backup: after extraction the save shows up in the SAVES list of Tabletop Simulator.
readme.importVault: Recommended install: open this .ttsmod file with TTS Mod Vault and import it.
readme.importManual: Manual install: extract this archive into the target directory (see next line).
readme.unzipTargetWarning: ⚠️ The extraction target is the PARENT directory of the Mods folder (the TTS data root), NOT the Mods folder itself!
readme.modsLayout: After extraction you should see a <target>/Mods/… layout; TTS Mod Vault picks the right location automatically.
readme.missingNote: Note: {count} asset(s) were missing when packing and are not included; Tabletop Simulator will try to download them again when loading those objects.

warning.packYamlMissing: Workspace has no pack.yaml; skipping the pack-name consistency check: {root}
warning.packNameMismatch: Import manifest declares pack name {manifestPack}, but pack.yaml says {packName} (warning only, nothing written back)
warning.unregisteredType: Object type {type} is not registered in the type registry; importing it as an open type: {name}
warning.skippedFiles: Deck {deck} skipped non-image files or subdirectories (not imported): {files}
warning.unmappedObjectFile: Object {name} field {field} could not be mapped to an objects.csv column; the file is still copied but not recorded in the ledger

tts_status.title: TTS status
tts_status.description: Query hub and TTS editor status: returns hub process info, TTS connection state, script engine version, and current save object count. Read-only, no side effects.

tts_pull.title: Pull scripts to workspace
tts_pull.description: Pull all in-game scripts and UI into the pack workspace at root (writes .lua / .xml files and creates directories). Writes local files only; does not modify anything in the game.

tts_exec.title: Execute Lua (has side effects)
tts_exec.description: Run a Lua snippet inside the TTS process and return its JSON result; defaults to the global script (guid -1). Has side effects: the snippet can read and change game state, so only run trusted code.

tts_assets.title: Asset URL liveness check
tts_assets.description: Check whether a list of asset URLs is reachable (HTTP probe): returns the total, alive/dead counts, and the dead list. Read-only network requests; writes no files.

tts_pack_list.title: List registered packs
tts_pack_list.description: List the packs registered in .registry.yaml; returns an empty list instead of an error when the registry is absent. Read-only.

tts_deck_slice.title: Slice deck atlas
tts_deck_slice.description: Slice a deck atlas into individual card images by grid and write them into outDir. Writes local files. When several decks match the atlas, pass deckKey or deckGuid to disambiguate; otherwise the call fails.

tts_deck_plan.title: Replacement plan (dry run)
tts_deck_plan.description: Dry-run replacement rules against a save JSON and list the affected URLs with statistics. Read-only; writes nothing.

tts_import.title: Import assets into workspace
tts_import.description: Import assets into a pack workspace according to an import.yaml manifest (writes local files). With dryRun=true it only validates the manifest and computes the import plan without touching disk.

tts_diff.title: Diff workspace vs game
tts_diff.description: Diff the local workspace against the in-game scripts/UI. Read-only: nothing is written or pushed.

tts_push.title: Push to game and reload (dangerous)
tts_push.description: Dangerous: writes workspace scripts/UI back into the game and triggers a reload (SaveAndPlay); entries without script/ui fields are deleted by TTS. Requires an explicit confirm=true; the call is rejected otherwise.
